claim: Approved immunotherapies are not available for the majority of cancer patients.
source: Despite success with cancer immunotherapies, approved immunotherapies are not available for the majority of cancer patients and only a minority of treated patients realize a durable response (Haslam and Prasad, 2019; Ben-Aharon et al., 2018; Darvin et al., 2018; Yang et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Haslam and Prasad, 2019; Ben-Aharon et al., 2018; Darvin et al., 2018; Yang et al., 2023).

claim: Only a minority of treated patients realize a durable response to immunotherapies.
source: Despite success with cancer immunotherapies, approved immunotherapies are not available for the majority of cancer patients and only a minority of treated patients realize a durable response (Haslam and Prasad, 2019; Ben-Aharon et al., 2018; Darvin et al., 2018; Yang et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Haslam and Prasad, 2019; Ben-Aharon et al., 2018; Darvin et al., 2018; Yang et al., 2023).

claim: Not all tumors with high indel mutational loads respond to checkpoint inhibitors.
source: While many studies correlate tumor insertion and deletion (indel) mutation load with immunotherapeutic response, not all tumors with high indel mutational loads respond to checkpoint inhibitors (Mandal et al., 2019; Turajlic et al., 2017; Yarchoan et al., 2017; Chan et al., 2019; Van Allen et al., 2015; Samstein et al., 2019; Ma et al., 2022; Rizvi et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Mandal et al., 2019; Turajlic et al., 2017; Yarchoan et al., 2017; Chan et al., 2019; Van Allen et al., 2015; Samstein et al., 2019; Ma et al., 2022; Rizvi et al., 2015).

claim: The typical adult solid tumor contains a median of 54 coding somatic nucleotide variants.
source: The typical adult solid tumor contains a median of 54 coding somatic nucleotide variants, many of which have the potential to create novel neoantigens or Mutation-Associated NeoAntigens (ICGC/TCGA Pan-Cancer Analysis of Whole Genomes Consortium, 2020; Vogelstein et al., 2013; Segal et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (ICGC/TCGA Pan-Cancer Analysis of Whole Genomes Consortium, 2020; Vogelstein et al., 2013; Segal et al., 2008).

claim: Approximately 5% of mutations are insertions/deletions (indels) or splice site changes that alter the open reading frame of the transcript.
source: Approximately 5% of mutations are insertions/deletions (indels) or splice site changes that alter the open reading frame of the transcript (ICGC/TCGA Pan-Cancer Analysis of Whole Genomes Consortium, 2020; Vogelstein et al., 2013; Segal et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (ICGC/TCGA Pan-Cancer Analysis of Whole Genomes Consortium, 2020; Vogelstein et al., 2013; Segal et al., 2008).

claim: Nonsense-mediated decay (NMD) plays an important role in messenger RNA (mRNA) quality control and normal gene expression.
source: In normal cells, nonsense-mediated decay (NMD) plays an important role in messenger RNA (mRNA) quality control, as well as normal gene expression (Frischmeyer and Dietz, 1999; Mendell et al., 2004; Carrard and Lejeune, 2023; Sun and Chen, 2023).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Frischmeyer and Dietz, 1999; Mendell et al., 2004; Carrard and Lejeune, 2023; Sun and Chen, 2023).

claim: NMD may aid immuno-evasion in cancer cells by eliminating RNA transcripts from genes that carry truncating mutants.
source: In cancer cells, however, NMD may aid immuno-evasion by eliminating RNA transcripts coming from genes that carry truncating mutants (Nogueira et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Nogueira et al., 2021).

claim: Knockdown of the NMD pathway with siRNA enhances the anti-tumor immune response.
source: Previous work has shown knockdown of the NMD pathway with small interfering RNA (siRNA) enhances the anti-tumor immune response (Pastor et al., 2010; Castle et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Pastor et al., 2010; Castle et al., 2014).

claim: Loss of UPF1 showed increased levels of aberrant transcripts and mutant proteins in alleles targeted by NMD.
source: Analysis of cell lines with loss of the UPF1 RNA helicase and ATPase gene (UPF1), a key mediator of NMD degradation, also showed increased levels of aberrant transcripts and mutant proteins in the alleles targeted by NMD (Oka et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Oka et al., 2021).

claim: There is no report of a specific chemical inhibitor of the NMD pathway with good bioavailability.
source: Despite early studies showing little toxicity with NMD inhibition, there is as of yet no reports of a specific chemical inhibitor of the pathway with good bioavailability (Martin et al., 2014; Durand et al., 2007; Zhao et al., 2022; Gotham et al., 2016; Gopalsamy et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Martin et al., 2014; Durand et al., 2007; Zhao et al., 2022; Gotham et al., 2016; Gopalsamy et al., 2012).

claim: A high-throughput assay was created to query the effects of a curated library of small molecules on NMD function.
source: In this work, we create a cell-based high-throughput assay to query the effects of a curated library of small molecules on NMD function.
evidence: Described as work performed in this study.

claim: A lead compound capable of inhibiting NMD was identified from the screen.
source: From this screen, we identify a lead compound capable of inhibiting NMD and ascertain its protein target as nonsense-mediated mRNA decay-associated phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)-related kinase (SMG1), a kinase that is a critical mediator of NMD.
evidence: Described as work performed in this study.

claim: The protein target of the lead compound is SMG1.
source: From this screen, we identify a lead compound capable of inhibiting NMD and ascertain its protein target as nonsense-mediated mRNA decay-associated phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)-related kinase (SMG1), a kinase that is a critical mediator of NMD.
evidence: Described as work performed in this study.

claim: A specific and bioavailable small molecule inhibitor of SMG1 (KVS0001) was designed.
source: As the lead compound produced unacceptable toxicity in animal models, we then designed a specific and bioavailable small molecule inhibitor of SMG1 (KVS0001) that is well-tolerated in vivo.
evidence: Described as work performed in this study.

claim: KVS0001 is well-tolerated in vivo.
source: As the lead compound produced unacceptable toxicity in animal models, we then designed a specific and bioavailable small molecule inhibitor of SMG1 (KVS0001) that is well-tolerated in vivo.
evidence: Described as work performed in this study.

claim: Targeted inhibition of SMG1 by KVS0001 leads to the presentation of novel neoantigens identifiable by T-cells.
source: We then demonstrate that targeted inhibition of SMG1 by KVS0001 leads to the presentation of novel neoantigens identifiable by T-cells leading to tumor growth inhibition in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: Described as work performed in this study.

claim: Targeted inhibition of SMG1 by KVS0001 leads to tumor growth inhibition in vitro and in vivo.
source: We then demonstrate that targeted inhibition of SMG1 by KVS0001 leads to the presentation of novel neoantigens identifiable by T-cells leading to tumor growth inhibition in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: Described as work performed in this study.

claim: Two genes, STAG2 and TP53, did not express their expected proteins when assessed by western blots or immunohistochemistry.
source: Through evaluation of this panel, we discovered two genes, Stromal Antigen 2 (STAG2) and Tumor Protein p53 (TP53), which did not express their expected proteins when assessed by western blots (STAG2) or immunohistochemistry (TP53) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The absence of STAG2 and TP53 proteins was suspected to be due to NMD because the inactivation was the result of frameshift mutations.
source: Because the inactivation of these two genes was the result of frameshift mutations, we suspected that the absence of the proteins was due to NMD.
evidence: Based on inference from the observation of frameshift mutations and protein absence.

claim: Whole transcriptome RNA-sequencing supported the suspicion that the absence of STAG2 and TP53 proteins was due to NMD.
source: This suspicion was supported by whole transcriptome RNA-sequencing (Figure 1—figure supplement 2; Cook et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by RNA-sequencing data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and cited work (Cook et al., 2022).

claim: STAG2 RNA transcripts decreased by 20-fold on average relative to wild-type transcripts in the parental cell lines.
source: Notably, we saw an average decrease of STAG2 RNA transcripts by 20-fold and TP53 by 6-fold relative to their respective wild-type transcripts in the parental cell lines.
evidence: Supported by RNA-sequencing data from the study.

claim: TP53 RNA transcripts decreased by 6-fold on average relative to wild-type transcripts in the parental cell lines.
source: Notably, we saw an average decrease of STAG2 RNA transcripts by 20-fold and TP53 by 6-fold relative to their respective wild-type transcripts in the parental cell lines.
evidence: Supported by RNA-sequencing data from the study.

claim: Treatment with emetine demonstrated up to a 60-fold recovery of mutant RNA transcript expression.
source: Treatment with the canonical protein synthesis inhibitor emetine, working indirectly to inhibit NMD, demonstrated up to a 60-fold recovery of mutant RNA transcript expression, establishing this panel as appropriate for HTS (Figure 1—figure supplement 3; Carter et al., 1995).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and citation (Carter et al., 1995).

claim: A next-generation sequencing (NGS) assay for NMD was designed.
source: We then designed a next-generation sequencing (NGS) assay for NMD (Figure 1A).
evidence: Described as work performed in this study and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The three cell lines were mixed in equal proportions and plated in 96-well plates followed by treatment with one compound per well.
source: We mixed the three cell lines in equal proportions and plated the mixture in 96-well plates followed by treatment with one compound (drug) per well.
evidence: Described as experimental method in this study.

claim: NMD inhibition efficacy was determined by comparing wild-type and truncating mutant transcript expression levels in a ratiometric manner.
source: We determined NMD inhibition efficacy by comparing the wild-type and truncating mutant transcript expression levels in a ratiometric manner.
evidence: Described as experimental method in this study.

claim: The wild-type sequences of the reciprocally knocked out clone served as internal references.
source: Specifically, the wild-type sequences of the reciprocally knocked out clone (i.e., wild-type STAG2 sequence from the TP53 knockout clones, and wild-type TP53 sequence from the STAG2 knockout clones) served as internal references, providing a ratiometric assay of mutant to wild-type transcript abundance.
evidence: Described as experimental method in this study.

claim: The ratiometric assay minimized confounders introduced by nonspecific transcriptional activators or generally toxic agents.
source: This ratiometric assay minimized confounders introduced by nonspecific transcriptional activators or generally toxic agents.
evidence: Based on inference from the design of the ratiometric assay.

claim: The use of three cell lines with different truncating mutations from two different target genes minimized the possibility that drugs identified in the HTS were cell line clone or mutation specific.
source: The use of three cell lines with different truncating mutations from two different target genes minimized the possibility that drugs identified in the HTS were cell line clone or mutation specific.
evidence: Based on inference from the experimental design.

claim: A combination of well and plate barcodes allowed the pooling and scoring of over 1920 assays in a single NGS lane.
source: A combination of well and plate barcodes allowed the pooling and scoring of over 1920 assays in a single NGS lane (see methods).
evidence: Described as experimental method in this study.

claim: Emetine and other well-known NMD inhibitors are unsuitable for human use due to off-target toxicity at doses required for NMD inhibition.
source: Previous human clinical trials suggest that off-target toxicity at doses required for NMD inhibition makes emetine and other well-known NMD inhibitors unsuitable for human use (Siddiqui et al., 1973; Moertel et al., 1974; Mastrangelo et al., 1973; Tang et al., 2012; Bongiorno et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Siddiqui et al., 1973; Moertel et al., 1974; Mastrangelo et al., 1973; Tang et al., 2012; Bongiorno et al., 2021).

claim: An HTS was performed to identify more specific NMD inhibitors by treating the isogenic cell line panel with a commercially available library consisting of 2658 FDA-approved or in late-phase clinical trial small molecules and natural products.
source: We performed an HTS to identify more specific NMD inhibitors by treating the isogenic cell line panel described above with a commercially available library consisting of 2658 FDA-approved or in late-phase clinical trial small molecules and natural products (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Described as experimental method in this study.

claim: Emetine increased the relative expression of mutant to wild-type transcripts by three- to fourfold on average.
source: Predictably, emetine increased the relative expression of mutant to wild-type transcripts by three- to fourfold on average (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: Eight compounds (0.3% of the library) increased the ratiometric mutant transcript fraction more than 5 standard deviations above the DMSO controls in all three cell lines.
source: Eight compounds (0.3% of the library) increased the ratiometric mutant transcript fraction more than 5 standard deviations above the dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) controls in all three cell lines (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Anisomycin is a known inhibitor of protein synthesis and commonly used NMD inhibitor for in vitro studies.
source: One of these eight compounds, anisomycin, is a known inhibitor of protein synthesis and commonly used NMD inhibitor for in vitro studies, providing independent validation of the screen (Carter et al., 1995).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Carter et al., 1995).

claim: Seven compounds increased mutant RNA transcript levels five- to tenfold relative to untreated cells.
source: The other seven compounds increased mutant RNA transcript levels five- to tenfold relative to untreated cells.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from the screen.

claim: Four of the original eight hit compounds increased mutant RNA expression in a dose-dependent manner in RPtec cells.
source: Four of the original eight hit compounds increased mutant RNA expression in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 8).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 8.

claim: Treatment with all four potential NMD inhibitors restored expression of the truncated mutant TP53 proteins.
source: While treatment with all four potential NMD inhibitors restored expression of the truncated mutant TP53 proteins, two of them (LY3023414 and halofuginone) did so most robustly (Figure 1D, E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and E.

claim: LY3023414 and halofuginone most robustly restored expression of the truncated mutant TP53 proteins.
source: While treatment with all four potential NMD inhibitors restored expression of the truncated mutant TP53 proteins, two of them (LY3023414 and halofuginone) did so most robustly (Figure 1D, E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and E.

claim: TP53 has an isoform, TP53β, whose expression is known to be controlled by the NMD pathway.
source: Additionally, TP53 has an isoform, TP53β, whose expression is known to be controlled by the NMD pathway (Cowen and Tang, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Cowen and Tang, 2017).

claim: An increase in the TP53β isoform was observed in cell lines treated with both LY3023414 and halofuginone.
source: Using cell lines with intact TP53β isoform transcripts, we observed an increase in the TP53β isoform in cell lines treated with both LY3023414 and halofuginone (Figure 1E, middle and left columns).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: qPCR confirmed the selective upregulation of TP53β, but not TP53α, transcripts in parental RPE1 and RPTec cells treated with LY3023414 or halofuginone.
source: Quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) of both the full-length TP53- (TP53α) and NMD-sensitive (TP53β) transcripts in parental RPE1 and RPTec cells treated with LY3023414 or halofuginone confirmed the selective upregulation of TP53β, but not TP53α, transcripts (Figure 1F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: LY3023414 was chosen to be the initial lead compound for further studies involving NMD inhibition based on a consistently stronger effect over halofuginone across multiple isogenic cell lines and assays.
source: Based on a consistently stronger effect of LY3023414 over halofuginone across multiple isogenic cell lines and assays, LY3023414 was chosen to be the initial lead compound for further studies involving NMD inhibition.
evidence: Based on inference from comparative experimental data.

claim: Treatment with LY3023414 followed by whole transcriptome RNA-sequencing revealed increased expression of the mutant allele in 42% and 67% of heterozygous, out-of-frame, indel mutations in NCI-H358 and LS180 cell lines, respectively.
source: Treatment with LY3023414 followed by whole transcriptome RNA-sequencing revealed increased expression of the mutant allele in 42% and 67% of heterozygous, out-of-frame, indel mutations in these two lines (Figure 2A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: A third of the nonsense mutations in NCI-H358 were recovered after treatment with LY3023414.
source: A third of the nonsense mutations in NCI-H358 were also 'recovered' (i.e., mutant transcripts increased relative to wild-type transcripts) after treatment with LY3023414 (Figure 2A, middle).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Single base pair substitutions not resulting in stop codons were not affected by LY3023414 in either NCI-H358 or LS180 cell lines.
source: Single base pair substitutions not resulting in stop codons were not affected by LY3023414 in either line (Figure 2A, right).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Targeted deep RNA-sequencing confirmed increased expression of the truncated mutant alleles relative to the wild-type alleles of the EXOC1 and SPTAN1 genes in NCI-H358 cells after treatment with LY3023414.
source: The whole transcriptome sequencing data were confirmed by targeted deep RNA-sequencing of two naturally occurring heterozygous truncating mutations from each cell line. Increased expression of the truncated mutant alleles relative to the wild-type alleles of the EXOC1 and SPTAN1 genes was observed in NCI-H358 cells after treatment with LY3023414 (Figure 2B, left).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Increased expression of HNRNPA3 and LRPPRC mutant transcripts was observed in LS180 after LY3023414 treatment.
source: Likewise, increased expression of HNRNPA3 and LRPPRC mutant transcripts was observed in LS180 after LY3023414 treatment (Figure 2B, right).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: No significant effects on two coding region heterozygous single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were noted after LY3023414 treatment in the genes RNF43 or DROSHA in either cell line.
source: We noted no significant effects on two coding region heterozygous single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) after LY3023414 treatment in the genes RNF43 or DROSHA in either cell line (Figure 2B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Western blotting revealed truncated mutant protein for both EXOC1 and SPTAN1 after treatment with LY3023414, whereas the full-length protein levels remained present and unchanged in both the treated and control samples.
source: To substantiate these transcriptomic effects at the protein level, we treated NCI-H358 cells for 24 hr with LY3023414. Western blotting revealed truncated mutant protein for both EXOC1 and SPTAN1 after treatment with LY3023414, whereas the full-length protein levels remained present and unchanged in both the treated and control (DMSO) samples (Figure 2C, D, left) (Williams et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C and D and citation (Williams et al., 2010).

claim: An antibody that recognizes the C-terminus of SPTAN1, encoded downstream of the frameshift mutation, did not detect mutant protein, as expected.
source: An antibody that recognizes the C-terminus of SPTAN1, encoded downstream of the frameshift mutation, did not detect mutant protein, as expected (Figure 2D, right).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and inference from the mutation location.

claim: LY3023414 was originally developed as a PI3K inhibitor with activity against AKT1 and mTOR.
source: LY3023414 was originally developed as a PI3K inhibitor with activity against AKT Serine/Threonine Kinase 1 (AKT1) and Mammalian Target of Rapamycin (mTOR) (Smith et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Smith et al., 2016).

claim: LY3023414 has been tested in a number of clinical trials and has a well-known pharmacokinetic profile in vivo.
source: It was tested in a number of clinical trials and has a well-known pharmacokinetic profile in vivo (Bendell et al., 2018; Rubinstein et al., 2020; Wei et al., 2016; Zou et al., 2017; Sweeney et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Bendell et al., 2018; Rubinstein et al., 2020; Wei et al., 2016; Zou et al., 2017; Sweeney et al., 2022).

claim: Treatment of mice with a single oral dose of 60 mg/kg LY3023414 led to a significant increase in the expression of mutant RNA transcripts relative to wild-type transcripts 16 hr later in NCI-H358 and LS180 xenograft tumors.
source: To determine whether LY3023414 affects NMD in vivo, we established xenograft tumors of both NCI-H358 and LS180 in nude mice. Treatment of these mice with a single oral dose of 60 mg/kg LY3023414 led to a significant increase in the expression of mutant RNA transcripts relative to wild-type transcripts 16 hr later (Figure 2E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The RNF43 gene, which harbors a coding region heterozygous SNP, served as a control in the in vivo experiment.
source: The RNF43 gene, which harbors a coding region heterozygous SNP, served as a control (Figure 2E).
evidence: Described as experimental design in this study and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Severe drug-associated toxicity, including weight loss bordering on cachexia and near total inactivity, precluded the longer-term dosing required for anti-tumorigenic effects of LY3023414 in both BALB/c and C57BL/6N immunocompetent mouse strains.
source: Severe drug-associated toxicity, including weight loss bordering on cachexia and near total inactivity, precluded the longer-term dosing required for anti-tumorigenic effects of LY3023414 in both BALB/c and C57BL/6N immunocompetent mouse strains.
evidence: Supported by experimental observations in this study.

claim: Only knockdown of SMG1 resulted in significant changes in the amount of truncating mutant transcript relative to wild-type transcript in all four genes evaluated.
source: siRNA-mediated knockdown of each of these kinases in NCI-H358 and LS180 cancer cell lines was performed for this purpose (Figure 3—figure supplement 1). Only knockdown of SMG1 resulted in significant changes in the amount of truncating mutant transcript relative to wild-type transcript in all four genes evaluated (Figure 3A, top).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: RNF43 and DROSHA contain heterozygous coding region SNPs and served as controls in the siRNA experiments and showed no changes despite siRNA treatment.
source: RNF43 and DROSHA contain heterozygous coding region SNPs and served as controls in these experiments and as expected showed no changes despite siRNA treatment (Figure 3A, bottom).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Knockdown of UPF1 with siRNA restored expression of the NMD-downregulated transcripts, at levels similar to those observed after the knockdown of SMG1.
source: SMG1 is known to regulate the NMD pathway by activating UPF1, an enzyme with RNA helicase and ATPase activity (Yamashita et al., 2001; Yamashita, 2013). We therefore knocked down UPF1 with siRNA and found that it restored expression of the NMD-downregulated transcripts, at levels similar to those observed after the knockdown of SMG1 (Figure 3B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and citations (Yamashita et al., 2001; Yamashita, 2013).

claim: Treatment of NCI-H358 and LS180 cancer cell lines with SMG1i-11 resulted in specific increases in the transcripts and proteins from genes with truncating mutations, just as did LY3023414.
source: Additionally, treatment of NCI-H358 and LS180 cancer cell lines with a previously reported SMG1-specific small molecule inhibitor, SMG1i-11, resulted in specific increases in the transcripts and proteins from genes with truncating mutations, just as did LY3023414 (Figure 3—figure supplements 2 and 3; Gopalsamy et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplements 2 and 3 and citation (Gopalsamy et al., 2012).

claim: SMG1i-11 was highly insoluble and could not be administered in vivo despite numerous attempts at various formulations and administration routes.
source: Although SMG1i-11 displayed considerable SMG1 specificity and marked inhibition of NMD, it was highly insoluble. While we had no difficulty getting it into solution in DMSO for in vitro work, we were unable to find a vehicle to administer it in vivo, despite numerous attempts at various formulations and administration routes.
evidence: Supported by experimental observations in this study.

claim: No peer-reviewed reports of SMG1i-11's in vivo activity have been reported to date, which may be explained by its insolubility.
source: This may explain why SMG1i-11 has been demonstrated to be an effective SMG1 inhibitor in vitro, but no peer-reviewed reports of its in vivo activity have been reported to date (Gopalsamy et al., 2012; Keenan et al., 2019; Valley et al., 2019).
evidence: Based on inference from the literature and experimental observations, supported by citations (Gopalsamy et al., 2012; Keenan et al., 2019; Valley et al., 2019).

claim: Eleven compounds (KVS0001 to KVS0011) were synthesized and tested for bioavailability and preservation of target specificity.
source: We sought to develop a new SMG1 inhibitor based on the cryo-electron microscopy structure of the binding pocket of SMG1 (Zhu et al., 2019; Langer et al., 2021). We attempted the synthesis of eleven compounds (KVS0001 to KVS0011) and tested for bioavailability and preservation of target specificity.
evidence: Described as work performed in this study, supported by citations (Zhu et al., 2019; Langer et al., 2021).

claim: KVS0001 stood out due to its solubility while preserving SMG1 inhibitory activity.
source: Among these, KVS0001 stood out due to its solubility while preserving SMG1 inhibitory activity (Supplementary file 3, Figure 3C, and Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: Mass spectrometry-based assays showed that KVS0001 inhibits SMG1 protein more than any of the other 246 protein or lipid kinases tested at concentrations from 10 nM to 1 µM.
source: Mass spectrometry-based assays showed that KVS0001 inhibits SMG1 protein more than any of the other 246 protein or lipid kinases tested at concentrations from 10 nM to 1 µM (Supplementary file 4 and Figure 3—figure supplement 5; Patricelli et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 5 and citation (Patricelli et al., 2011).

claim: Noteworthy off-target kinase inhibition by KVS0001 was not observed until doses of 1 µM and above.
source: Noteworthy off-target kinase inhibition was not observed until doses of 1 µM and above.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from mass spectrometry-based assays.

claim: KVS0001 is bioactive in the nanomolar range and subverts the NMD-mediated downregulation of truncating mutant transcripts and proteins in NCI-H358 and LS180 cells.
source: Experiments using NCI-H358 and LS180 cells showed that KVS0001 is bioactive in the nanomolar range and subverts the NMD-mediated downregulation of truncating mutant transcripts and proteins (Figure 3D, E, Figure 3—figure supplements 6 and 7).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D, E, Figure 3—figure supplements 6 and 7.

claim: Inhibition at concentrations as low as 600 nM led to equal expression of wild-type and mutant transcripts, suggesting near total blockade of the NMD pathway.
source: Inhibition at concentrations as low as 600 nM led to equal expression of wild-type and mutant transcripts, suggesting near total blockade of the NMD pathway (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 6).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 6.

claim: Western blotting showed that KVS0001 substantially decreases the amount of phosphorylated UPF1, the downstream target of SMG1 kinase activity, in three different cell lines.
source: Western blotting showed that KVS0001 substantially decreases the amount of phosphorylated UPF1, the downstream target of SMG1 kinase activity, in three different cell lines (Figure 3F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: KVS0001 treatment of NCI-H358- and LS180-derived xenograft tumors in nude mice resulted in significant increases in transcript levels in each of six tested endogenous genes with truncating mutations.
source: Finally, KVS0001 treatment of NCI-H358- and LS180-derived xenograft tumors in nude mice resulted in significant increases in transcript levels in each of six tested endogenous genes with truncating mutations, while having had no measurable effects on genes containing heterozygous coding region SNPs (Figure 3G, H).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G and H.

claim: KVS0001 had no measurable effects on genes containing heterozygous coding region SNPs in xenograft tumors.
source: Finally, KVS0001 treatment of NCI-H358- and LS180-derived xenograft tumors in nude mice resulted in significant increases in transcript levels in each of six tested endogenous genes with truncating mutations, while having had no measurable effects on genes containing heterozygous coding region SNPs (Figure 3G, H).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G and H.

claim: Previous studies with non-specific or toxic NMD inhibitors have shown an increase in selected antigens from tumor-specific mutations when NMD is inhibited.
source: Indeed, previous studies with non-specific or toxic NMD inhibitors have shown an increase in selected antigens from tumor-specific mutations when NMD is inhibited (Becker et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Becker et al., 2021).

claim: Using quantitative HPLC-MS, a striking (45- to 90-fold) increase in the EXOC1- and RAB14-derived neoantigens, and a significant (twofold) increase in the ZDHHC16-derived neoantigen was observed in NCI-H358 and LS180 cells treated with KVS0001.
source: Using quantitative high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC)–mass spectrometry (MS) we observed a striking (45- to 90-fold) increase in the EXOC1- and RAB14-derived neoantigens, and a significant (twofold) increase in the ZDHHC16-derived neoantigen (Figure 4A, B, Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2; Wang et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A, B, Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2, and citation (Wang et al., 2019).

claim: The increase in neoantigen presentation is consistent with the re-expression of mutant transcript and protein shown previously in this study.
source: This is consistent with the re-expression of mutant transcript and protein shown previously in this study (Figure 3D, E).
evidence: Based on inference from previous experimental data shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: NCI-H716 and NCI-H2228 both contain homozygous mutations in TP53 which produce transcripts downregulated by NMD, with each exhibiting RNA levels less than 20% of the median level of expression among 675 cancer cell lines.
source: Both lines contain homozygous mutations in TP53 which produce transcripts downregulated by NMD, with each exhibiting RNA levels less than 20% of the median level of expression among 675 cancer cell lines (Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 3; Lindeboom et al., 2016; Klijn et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 3, and citations (Lindeboom et al., 2016; Klijn et al., 2015).

claim: Treatment with KVS0001 increased the expression of TP53 protein in both NCI-H716 and NCI-H2228 cell lines.
source: Treatment with KVS0001 increased the expression of TP53 protein in both lines, while the commonly used therapeutic agents 5-fluorouracil and etoposide did not affect TP53 abundance (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: The commonly used therapeutic agents 5-fluorouracil and etoposide did not affect TP53 abundance in NCI-H716 and NCI-H2228 cell lines.
source: Treatment with KVS0001 increased the expression of TP53 protein in both lines, while the commonly used therapeutic agents 5-fluorouracil and etoposide did not affect TP53 abundance (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: A bispecific antibody (KVS-BI043) was developed that recognizes a peptide–HLA complex on one end and CD3 on the other end.
source: To determine whether this disruption of NMD repression is targetable by T-cells, we developed a bispecific antibody (KVS-BI043) that recognizes a peptide–HLA complex on one end and CD3 on the other end.
evidence: Described as work performed in this study.

claim: KVS-BI043 recognizes a ten amino acid peptide (residues 125–134 of TP53) bound to HLA-A24.
source: KVS-BI043 recognizes a ten amino acid peptide (residues 125–134 of TP53) bound to HLA-A24.
evidence: Described as work performed in this study.

claim: Treatment of NCI-H716_A24 or NCI-H2228 cells with KVS0001 and the KVS-BI043 bispecific antibody in the presence of normal T-cells caused a significant increase in IFN-γ release.
source: Treatment of NCI-H716_A24 or NCI-H2228 cells with KVS0001 and the KVS-BI043 bispecific antibody in the presence of normal T-cells caused a significant increase in interferon (IFN-γ) release (Figure 4E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: No changes in IFN-γ levels were observed in the absence of KVS-BI043 or normal T-cells.
source: We observed no changes in IFN-γ levels in the absence of KVS-BI043 or normal T-cells (Figure 4E, gray boxed lanes).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Treatment of NCI-H716_A24 with KVS0001 in the presence of KVS-BI043 and T-cells led to significant killing of the target cancer cells.
source: Most importantly, treatment of NCI-H716_A24 with KVS0001 in the presence of KVS-BI043 and T-cells led to significant killing of the target cancer cells, which was also not observed in the absence of T-cells or the absence of HLA-24 in the target cells (Figure 4F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Killing was not observed in the absence of T-cells or the absence of HLA-24 in the target cells.
source: Most importantly, treatment of NCI-H716_A24 with KVS0001 in the presence of KVS-BI043 and T-cells led to significant killing of the target cancer cells, which was also not observed in the absence of T-cells or the absence of HLA-24 in the target cells (Figure 4F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: NCI-H2228 was assessed for killing but expressed too much TP53 at baseline and thus displayed substantial killing even in the DMSO controls.
source: NCI-H2228 was assessed for killing but expressed too much TP53 at baseline (Figure 4D, left most lane) and thus displayed substantial killing even in the DMSO controls.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Six of the twelve truncating mutation-containing genes and five of the six expression controlled by NMD genes had significantly increased RNA following in vitro treatment with KVS0001 in LLC and RENCA cells.
source: For this purpose, we tested eight genes in LLC, and four in RENCA, which contained out-of-frame indel mutations potentially targeted by NMD. We also assessed the expression of three genes without any mutations known to have their normal expression controlled by NMD (Echols et al., 2020). We found that six of the twelve truncating mutation-containing genes and five of the six expression controlled by NMD genes had significantly increased RNA following in vitro treatment with KVS0001 (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and B, and citation (Echols et al., 2020).

claim: Both LLC and RENCA tumor types experienced significant slowing of tumor growth when treated with KVS0001 in immune-competent mice.
source: We then implanted LLC and RENCA cancer cells in the mammary fat pad of C57BL/6N and BALB/c mice, respectively, and treated with KVS0001 or vehicle control (Figure 5C). The dose of KVS0001 was based on experiments showing that the maximum solubility limit was reached around 2–3 mg/ml, leading to a maximum single dose of 30 mg/kg per mouse per treatment. At this dose, the only toxicity noted was transient weight loss (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), and no other pathology was observed. Both tumor types experienced significant slowing of tumor growth (Figure 5D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C, D, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: At the dose of 30 mg/kg KVS0001, the only toxicity noted was transient weight loss, and no other pathology was observed.
source: At this dose, the only toxicity noted was transient weight loss (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), and no other pathology was observed.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: When LLC and RENCA tumors were implanted in immunocompromised mice, there was no statistically significant difference in tumor growth between mice treated with KVS0001 or vehicle control.
source: However, when the same tumors were implanted in immunocompromised mice, there was no statistically significant difference in tumor growth between mice treated with KVS0001 or vehicle control (Figure 5E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: None of the three models with moderate or low numbers of truncating mutations responded to KVS0001 (EMT6, B16-F10, M3 Melanoma).
source: We evaluated a total of seven syngeneic mouse cancer cell lines. Four contained a relatively high number of truncating indel mutations, while the remaining three contained a moderate or low number. None of the three models with moderate or low numbers of truncating mutations responded to KVS0001 (EMT6, B16-F10, M3 Melanoma) (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Of the four models with a higher number of truncating mutations, two (LLC and RENCA) responded in a statistically significant fashion while the other two failed to reach significance (CT26, MC38).
source: Of the four models with a higher number of truncating mutations, two (LLC and RENCA) responded in a statistically significant fashion while the other two failed to reach significance (CT26, MC38) (Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The method employs a ratiometric output, allowing quantitative and controlled determination of RNA expression changes associated with NMD.
source: The method employs a ratiometric output, allowing quantitative and controlled determination of RNA expression changes associated with NMD.
evidence: Described as a feature of the method developed in this study.

claim: Unlike previous NMD screens, this assay is directed at NMD as a process rather than as a way to identify compounds for treating specific mutations related to a disease state.
source: Unlike previous NMD screens, this assay is directed at NMD as a process rather than as a way to identify compounds for treating specific mutations related to a disease state, such as cystic fibrosis or β-thalassemia (Martin et al., 2014; Zhao et al., 2022; Salvatori et al., 2009).
evidence: Based on comparison with previous screens, supported by citations (Martin et al., 2014; Zhao et al., 2022; Salvatori et al., 2009).

claim: The genetically modified isogenic cell lines employed here are uniquely suited for this approach, producing a high signal-to-noise ratio.
source: The genetically modified isogenic cell lines employed here are uniquely suited for this approach, producing a high signal-to-noise ratio.
evidence: Based on inference from the experimental design.

claim: Four of the eight hits re-expressed transcripts from genes with truncating mutations in a dose-responsive manner when re-tested, confirming a low false positive rate in the screen.
source: Follow-up experiments confirmed a low false positive rate in the screen: four of the eight hits re-expressed transcripts from genes with truncating mutations in a dose-responsive manner when re-tested.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from validation experiments.

claim: The assay allows for the detection of NMD inhibitors regardless of effects on protein translation by virtue of the comparison of wild-type to mutant transcripts for each queried gene.
source: Note that our assay allows for the detection of NMD inhibitors regardless of effects on protein translation by virtue of the comparison of wild-type to mutant transcripts for each queried gene.
evidence: Based on inference from the experimental design.

claim: Many previously reported inhibitors of NMD, such as emetine and anisomycin, rely on inhibition of protein translation and thus are unlikely to be optimal for specific restoration of NMD-targeted RNA and protein expression.
source: This is an important feature, as many previously reported inhibitors of NMD, such as emetine and anisomycin, rely on inhibition of protein translation and thus are unlikely to be optimal for specific restoration of NMD-targeted RNA and protein expression (Siddiqui et al., 1973; Tang et al., 2012; Bongiorno et al., 2021; Bhuvanagiri et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Siddiqui et al., 1973; Tang et al., 2012; Bongiorno et al., 2021; Bhuvanagiri et al., 2014).

claim: Different NMD inhibitors caused re-expression of different knockout clones to different extents.
source: During the review process, it was also noted that different NMD inhibitors caused re-expression of different knockout clones to different extents (see Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 8 as an example).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 8.

claim: It is speculated that the differential re-expression by different NMD inhibitors may be related to differences in the mechanism of action.
source: It is not clear to us why this occurred, but we speculate that it may be related to differences in the mechanism of action (i.e., protein synthesis inhibition-based NMD effects versus targeted NMD pathway inhibition as one example).
evidence: Based on speculation about the mechanism of action.

claim: SMG1 acts as the gatekeeper of UPF1 activity through its phosphorylation at multiple sites.
source: SMG1 acts as the gatekeeper of UPF1 activity through its phosphorylation at multiple sites (Yamashita et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Yamashita et al., 2001).

claim: Issues likely related to off-target (pan-kinase) toxicity at the doses required for NMD inhibition prevented LY3023414 from being utilized in further in vivo work.
source: Unfortunately, issues likely related to off-target (pan-kinase) toxicity at the doses required for NMD inhibition prevented LY3023414 from being utilized in further in vivo work.
evidence: Based on inference from experimental observations.

claim: All previously described SMG1 inhibitors have undesirable off-target or biophysical characteristics complicating their use as therapeutic agents.
source: While there are previously described SMG1 inhibitors, all have undesirable off-target or biophysical characteristics complicating their use as therapeutic agents (Martin et al., 2014; Durand et al., 2007; Zhao et al., 2022; Gotham et al., 2016; Bongiorno et al., 2021; Becker et al., 2021; Cheruiyot et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Martin et al., 2014; Durand et al., 2007; Zhao et al., 2022; Gotham et al., 2016; Bongiorno et al., 2021; Becker et al., 2021; Cheruiyot et al., 2018).

claim: The screen offered an unbiased assessment of the best targets for NMD pathway disruption, and thus SMG1 was concluded to be an ideal protein to inhibit for this purpose.
source: Despite these chemistry-related challenges, our screen offered an unbiased assessment of the best targets for NMD pathway disruption, and thus we concluded that SMG1 was an ideal protein to inhibit for this purpose.
evidence: Based on inference from the screen results.

claim: KVS0001 was a specific inhibitor of SMG1 that was soluble and could easily be administered to mice.
source: In light of this, we attempted to improve the biophysical properties of SMG1i-11 through the development of KVS0001. As reported in this study, KVS0001 was a specific inhibitor of SMG1 that was soluble and could easily be administered to mice.
evidence: Described as work performed in this study.

claim: Treatment of KVS0001 not only increased levels of transcripts and proteins from genes with truncating mutations, but also increased the levels of corresponding peptide bound–HLA complexes on the cell surfaces.
source: Treatment of KVS0001 not only increased levels of transcripts and proteins from genes with truncating mutations, but also increased the levels of corresponding peptide bound–HLA complexes on the cell surfaces.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from the study.

claim: A new bispecific antibody, KVS-B043, was developed which could recognize pHLA complexes when the truncating mutations were present in the TP53 gene and destroy cancer cells harboring such mutations.
source: We developed a new bispecific antibody, KVS-B043, which could recognize these pHLA complexes when the truncating mutations were present in the TP53 gene and destroy cancer cells harboring such mutations.
evidence: Described as work performed in this study.

claim: In syngeneic mouse models, KVS0001 slowed the growth of some tumors containing multiple truncating mutations, but only when the mice were immunocompetent.
source: In syngeneic mouse models, KVS0001 slowed the growth of some tumors containing multiple truncating mutations, but only when the mice were immunocompetent.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from the study.

claim: The dependence on an intact immune system supports the idea that the slowed growth of the treated tumors was due to recognition of neoantigens.
source: This dependence on an intact immune system supports the idea that the slowed growth of the treated tumors was due to recognition of neoantigens.
evidence: Based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: It is not understood why KVS0001 (and other NMD inhibitors) increase the expression of many, but not all, genes with truncating mutations.
source: Despite these encouraging data, the potential utility of KVS0001 for therapeutic purposes remains speculative, for several reasons. First, we do not understand why KVS0001 (and other NMD inhibitors) increase the expression of many, but not all, genes with truncating mutations.
evidence: Acknowledged as a limitation of current understanding.

claim: The changes to splicing that are undoubtedly occurring when NMD is disrupted in either normal or tumor tissue are not systematically addressed.
source: We also do not systematically address the changes to splicing that are undoubtedly occurring when NMD is disrupted in either normal or tumor tissue.
evidence: Acknowledged as a limitation of the study.

claim: Treatment with KVS0001 reduced the growth of some but not all syngeneic tumor types tested in mice.
source: Second, treatment with KVS0001 reduced the growth of some but not all syngeneic tumor types tested in mice.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from the study.

claim: There appeared to be a correlation between the ability of KVS0001 to inhibit growth and the number of truncating mutations in the tumor.
source: There appeared to be a correlation between the ability of KVS0001 to inhibit growth and the number of truncating mutations in the tumor.
evidence: Based on inference from experimental data.

claim: Recent evidence has been presented showing that cells deficient in known splicing factors are sensitive to subsequent NMD inhibition.
source: Likewise, recent evidence has been presented showing that cells deficient in known splicing factors are sensitive to subsequent NMD inhibition (Cheruiyot, 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Cheruiyot, 2021).

claim: The situation with KVS0001 is reminiscent of that encountered with immune checkpoint inhibitors, in which there is a positive but imperfect correlation with loss of microsatellite instability-related proteins and tumor mutation burden.
source: This situation is reminiscent of that encountered with immune checkpoint inhibitors, in which there is a positive but imperfect correlation with loss of microsatellite instability-related proteins and tumor mutation burden (Yarchoan et al., 2017; Ma et al., 2022).
evidence: Based on comparison with checkpoint inhibitors, supported by citations (Yarchoan et al., 2017; Ma et al., 2022).

claim: The ability of the immune system to react to neoantigens is related to their quality as well as their quantity, with quality defined as the ability of the neoantigen to be bound to the host's particular MHC constitution and initiate an immune response.
source: Undoubtedly, the ability of the immune system to react to neoantigens is related to their quality as well as their quantity, with quality defined as the ability of the neoantigen to be bound to the host's particular MHC constitution and initiate an immune response (Halima et al., 2022; Ribas and Wolchok, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Halima et al., 2022; Ribas and Wolchok, 2018).

claim: Treatment with KVS0001 led to decreased tumor growth in immunocompetent mice, but did not lead to tumor regressions of the type mandated by RECIST criteria in human clinical trials.
source: Third, treatment with KVS0001 led to decreased tumor growth in immunocompetent mice, but did not lead to tumor regressions of the type mandated by RECIST criteria in human clinical trials (Eisenhauer et al., 2009; Seymour et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from the study and citations (Eisenhauer et al., 2009; Seymour et al., 2017).

claim: Whether the failure to cure tumors in mice results from the contrived nature of the models used complicates the interpretation of many pre-clinical immunotherapeutic approaches.
source: Whether this failure to cure tumors in mice results from the contrived nature of the models used – injection of large numbers of rapidly growing cancer cells into animals with relatively little time to react prior to their demise – complicates the interpretation of many pre-clinical immunotherapeutic approaches.
evidence: Based on speculation about the limitations of pre-clinical models.

claim: KVS0001, though it was soluble and could be administered to animals for at least a month, was not entirely non-toxic, causing transient weight loss in some of the mice.
source: Finally, KVS0001, though it was soluble and could be administered to animals for at least a month, was not entirely non-toxic, causing transient weight loss in some of the mice.
evidence: Supported by experimental observations in the study.

claim: Previous work has raised concerns that the importance of NMD in development and normal gene expression make it a difficult pathway to safely disrupt.
source: Previous work has raised concerns that the importance of NMD in development and normal gene expression make it a difficult pathway to safely disrupt (Mendell et al., 2004; Kurosaki et al., 2019; Tarpey et al., 2007; Nguyen et al., 2013; McIlwain et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Mendell et al., 2004; Kurosaki et al., 2019; Tarpey et al., 2007; Nguyen et al., 2013; McIlwain et al., 2010).

claim: The limited impact on body weight or observed physical activity of mice undergoing KVS0001 therapy at therapeutically relevant doses suggests that NMD inhibition may have acceptable toxicity and be tolerated in developed animals.
source: The limited impact on body weight or observed physical activity of mice undergoing KVS0001 therapy at therapeutically relevant doses suggests that NMD inhibition may have acceptable toxicity and be tolerated in developed animals.
evidence: Based on inference from experimental observations.

claim: Natural genetic variants of NMD components convey variability in the efficiency of NMD between humans, and lends itself to supporting that knockdown of this pathway may be tolerable.
source: Another example of this lies in the natural genetic variants of NMD components, which convey variability in the efficiency of NMD between humans, and lends itself to supporting that knockdown of this pathway may be tolerable (Linde et al., 2007; Nguyen et al., 2014; MacArthur et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Linde et al., 2007; Nguyen et al., 2014; MacArthur et al., 2012).

claim: Studies in mice support the observation that post-development knockdown of UPF1 displayed minimal phenotype change.
source: Studies in mice also support this observation, as post-development knockdown of UPF1 displayed minimal phenotype change (Echols et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Echols et al., 2020).

claim: The broad use of NMD in normal development and growth, coupled with the observations here, suggests future work with inhibitors of this pathway should continue with a close eye for on-target off-tissue toxicity.
source: The broad use of NMD in normal development and growth, coupled with the observations here, suggests future work with inhibitors of this pathway should continue with a close eye for on-target off-tissue toxicity.
evidence: Based on inference from the experimental observations and known biology.

claim: The potential use of KVS0001 to prevent the onset of symptoms in pediatric syndromes caused by germline truncating mutations is speculated.
source: Should the administration of KVS0001 or a related compound prove non-toxic and well tolerated in humans, we end with a speculation about the possibility of KVS0001 being used as a preventative rather than as a therapeutic agent. Its potential use to prevent the onset of symptoms in pediatric syndromes caused by germline truncating mutations is obvious (Lindeboom et al., 2019; Miller and Pearce, 2014).
evidence: Based on speculation about potential applications, supported by citations (Lindeboom et al., 2019; Miller and Pearce, 2014).

claim: The potential for KVS0001 to prophylactically reduce cancer incidence in patients with hereditary non-polyposis colorectal cancer is speculated.
source: Less obvious is the potential for it to prophylactically reduce cancer incidence in patients with hereditary non-polyposis colorectal cancer. These patients inherit heterozygous mutations of a mismatch repair gene, and they do not develop tumors until biallelic mutations of that mismatch repair gene are acquired in a rare stem cell during the second or third decade of life.
evidence: Based on speculation about potential applications.

claim: Similar speculations can be made about the potential of KVS0001 to be used to prevent cancer initiation or progression in patients with other inherited mutations in repair genes, or in individuals exposed to high levels of exogenous mutagens.
source: Similar speculations can be made about the potential of KVS0001 to be used to prevent cancer initiation or progression in patients with other inherited mutations in repair genes, or in individuals exposed to high levels of exogenous mutagens.
evidence: Based on speculation about potential applications.
